summary.prose: The index no longer misses files in directories that are created together with their parent. When the watcher sees a new directory that has subdirectories, it adds a watch for that directory and then reports every file already in it, so the files reach the index and later writes are seen too. As a backstop for what the watcher cannot know about, the code-review freshness check also asks for any stale changed file the index holds to be indexed once per modification time, treats a deleted file or a file the index never holds as not stale, and never calls a file fresh that is still stale after its request, so a file that cannot be indexed ends in the existing degraded diff review. The review-session timeout seen on 2026-10-27 is a different defect handled elsewhere and is not part of this Story.

boundary.internal: Index changed files the watcher misses and let the code-review freshness gate request them

api.name: Watcher.addRepo

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Absolute path of the repo to watch

parameters.name: ignore
parameters.purpose: Directory names to leave out of the watch, the scan and the per-directory watches; defaults to IGNORE_DIRS

returns.meaning: Resolves once the repo subscription exists; unchanged

errors.type: error thrown by the watcher backend
errors.condition: The repo subscription cannot be created, as today

postconditions: For each create event whose path is a directory, not a symbolic link, and with no ignored segment below the repo root, and that has no subscription of its own yet: if the directory has subdirectories, a recursive subscription for it is created first; then a create event is emitted for every file in its tree, skipping ignored directories and symbolic links

A directory whose subscription fails is logged and still scanned, so its files are reported once

api.name: computeCodeReviewFreshness
api.signature: (repoPath: string, changedFiles: readonly string[], deps: FreshnessDeps) => Promise<FreshnessResult>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Absolute path of the registered repo

parameters.name: changedFiles
parameters.purpose: The Story's changed files, repo-relative or absolute

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Read-only seams; gains selection and requestedAt

returns.meaning: The existing fields plus unindexedFiles: the stale files that exist and that the index holds (they have entities with an older watermark, or they are selected files without entities), and that have not been requested at or after their current mtime

errors.type: none thrown by the compute itself
errors.condition: A selection read that throws keeps an entity-less file stale and unlisted; a file whose mtime reads as 0 (deleted or unstattable) is settled first and is never stale on its own, as today

preconditions: deps.codeIndexWork, entityWatermark, repoLastIndexed, fileMtime, selection and requestedAt are provided
postconditions: A changed file whose mtime is 0 is not in staleFiles or unindexedFiles, selection is not consulted for it, and nothing is requested for it
A file with an entity watermark keeps its comparison: it is stale exactly when the watermark is older than its mtime; selection is not consulted for it
A file with an entity watermark that is stale is in unindexedFiles unless requestedAt is at or after its mtime
A file that exists, has no entities and has selection 'not-code' or 'excluded-by-ignore' is not in staleFiles

A file that exists, has no entities and has selection 'selected' is always in staleFiles, whatever the repo-level lastIndexed or any earlier request, and is in unindexedFiles unless requestedAt is at or after its mtime
The compute performs no write and queues nothing

dataModelChanges.details: A Map in the Watcher from the absolute path of a directory that was created together with subdirectories to its @parcel/watcher subscription, with the ignore list of its repo held per repo. Entries are added on a create event, removed on a delete event for that directory, and cleared by removeRepo and close. In memory only; empty after a restart, where the start-up delta pass covers files changed while the daemon was down.

selection: (repoPath: string, file: string) => Promise<FileSelection> ; requestedAt: (repoPath: string, file: string) => number | undefined (unix ms of the last index request for the file, from a daemon-side map that lives for the daemon process)
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
+ readonly selection: (repoPath: string, file: string) => Promise<FileSelection>;
+ readonly requestedAt: (repoPath: string, file: string) => number | undefined;

dataModelChanges.details: unindexedFiles: readonly string[], a subset of staleFiles. Additive: the controller-side handler reads isProcessing, inFlight, pendingCodeIndexJobs and staleFiles and ignores the new field.

A Map from absolute file path to the unix ms of the last request, held in the codeReview.freshness handler's closure in handler-runtime. Not persisted; empty after a daemon restart, which only means a file is requested once more.

errorCases.scenario: The per-directory subscription for a new directory cannot be created (an inotify limit, a permission error, the directory removed first)
errorCases.detection: The subscribe call rejects and the watcher catches the rejection
errorCases.response: A warning with the directory is logged, no entry is kept for it, and the scan still reports the files present, so they are indexed once
errorCases.userImpact: Files written later in that directory are not seen by the watcher; the freshness gate still requests them when a review asks, and the start-up delta pass covers them after a restart

errorCases.scenario: The scan of a new directory fails part-way (a subdirectory removed or unreadable during the walk)
errorCases.detection: A readdir or lstat call throws for one entry
errorCases.response: That entry is skipped, the rest of the tree is reported, and a debug line is logged
errorCases.userImpact: At most the files under the unreadable entry are not reported by the scan

errorCases.scenario: The daemon handler cannot queue the file job for a stale file (the queue is stopped, as during shutdown)
errorCases.detection: queue.enqueue returns without queueing, so the re-read of the queue state after the request still shows no code index work
errorCases.response: The file stays stale; it is not declared fresh
errorCases.userImpact: The gate waits for the freshness time-out and the review runs as a degraded diff review

errorCases.scenario: A listed file is requested but the indexer throws on it or leaves it without a fresh File entity (a parse failure, an unregistered repo)
errorCases.detection: After the job ends, the next poll finds the file still stale and the queue idle
errorCases.response: The file stays stale and is not requested again for the same mtime
errorCases.userImpact: The gate waits for the freshness time-out, then the review runs as a degraded diff review, which does not depend on graph entities for that file

errorCases.scenario: The selection seam throws for a changed file that exists and has no entities
errorCases.detection: The compute catches an exception from deps.selection for that file
errorCases.response: The file is treated as selected and kept stale, but it is not listed in unindexedFiles, so nothing is queued for it
errorCases.userImpact: The gate may wait for the freshness time-out for that file and then fall back to the degraded diff review

errorCases.scenario: A changed file cannot be stat'ed (it was deleted, or a permission error)
errorCases.detection: The real fileMtime catches the statSync failure and returns 0
errorCases.response: The compute settles the file before any entity or selection read: it is not stale, not listed as unindexed and nothing is requested, as today
errorCases.userImpact: A deleted source file never holds the gate or queues an index job for a path that does not exist

invariantsToPreserve.text: The repo subscription, its ignore list, the 200 ms debounce and the handlers' view of events as {type, path} are unchanged; a file event from a per-directory subscription is indistinguishable from one from the repo subscription
A directory created alone, or a child created later than its parent, is already watched by the repo subscription, so it gets no second subscription
The Indexer drops events whose extension is not supported and a queued file job for the same path replaces the earlier one, so repeated events cost nothing
A changed file with indexed entities is stale exactly when its newest entity indexedAt is older than the file's mtime, and the compute never writes or queues anything
A changed file that cannot be stat'ed has mtime 0 and is never stale on its own
A file with a parser leaves a File entity when indexed, and a file event deletes the file's old entities before writing the new ones; selectFile stays the one rule for what the index holds

The controller-side handler keeps reading isProcessing, inFlight, pendingCodeIndexJobs and staleFiles with the same meaning, and its freshness time-out and diff-only fallback are unchanged; the full review falls back to the diff review only when grounding has no symbols at all, so a file left out of the graph in a mixed set must be kept stale rather than reported fresh
The handler, routing, long-review, RPC fallback and review-stream-freshness tests, which fake the freshness result, keep passing without edits

migration.stateBefore: The Watcher holds one @parcel/watcher subscription per repo and hands its events to the Indexer (bundle c1). On Linux, a directory created together with its parent is never watched, so files written into it, even much later, produce no event until the daemon restarts and its start-up delta pass re-queues them (bundle c2). The freshness check judges a changed file with entities by its watermark and a file without entities by the repo-level lastIndexed, which is also set at start-up before the delta jobs finish (bundles c3 and c4); nothing in the gate asks for indexing and the codeReview.freshness handler is read-only (bundle c5). A deleted file has mtime 0 and is never stale today.
migration.stateAfter: The Watcher gives each new directory that has subdirectories its own subscription, created before its tree is scanned, and reports the files already in it; the subscription is released when the directory is deleted, on removeRepo and on close, and a failed subscription is logged with the scan kept. The freshness check settles a file with mtime 0 first, classes an entity-less file with selectFile, lists every stale file the index holds as unindexed, and the codeReview.freshness handler queues one file job for it per mtime and re-reads the queue; a file still stale after its request stays stale, so the existing freshness time-out sends the review to the degraded diff review. FreshnessResult has one more field, unindexedFiles. No stored data changes.

migrationSteps.action: Change the Watcher so a create event for a directory under a watched repo adds its own subscription when it has subdirectories, then scans the tree and emits create events for its files, with the per-directory subscriptions released on delete, removeRepo and close

Add the selection and requestedAt seams to FreshnessDeps and the unindexedFiles field to FreshnessResult, and the new rules to the compute with the mtime-0 case settled first and every stale held file listed, with the real selection seam in realFreshnessGraphDeps

In the codeReview.freshness handler, keep the in-memory request map, supply requestedAt from it, queue one file job for each file in unindexedFiles, record the time, and re-read the queue state for the reply

Add the watcher integration test and the freshness unit, integration and contract tests, update the existing whole-result assertions in freshness.test.ts, and run the handler, routing, long-review, RPC fallback and review-stream-freshness tests unchanged

Rebuild and restart the daemon so the running process uses the new watcher and handler; the per-directory subscriptions and the request map start empty, and the start-up delta pass covers files changed while it was down

migration.backwardCompat: The Watcher keeps its public methods and the {type, path} event shape, so the Indexer and both places that construct a Watcher need no change; only the set of events grows, by create events for files in directories the watcher previously did not cover. The freshness IPC reply only gains unindexedFiles; clients that read isProcessing, inFlight, pendingCodeIndexJobs and staleFiles are unaffected, and the controller-side wait loop, its freshness time-out and the diff-only fallback are unchanged. A client talking to an older daemon sees no unindexedFiles and the old behaviour.

alternativesConsidered.name: Close the watcher blind spot with a per-directory watch and a scan, and keep the gate's index request as a backstop
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The watcher watches and scans every new directory that has subdirectories, so the index stays current; the freshness gate also requests indexing of any stale file the index holds.
alternativesConsidered.approach: In the Watcher, a create event for a directory under a watched repo (not on the ignore list) first adds a dedicated recursive subscription for that directory when it has subdirectories, then walks the new tree and emits a create event for each file in it; the subscription is released on delete, removeRepo and close, and a failure to subscribe is logged with the scan kept. Separately, the freshness compute lists every stale changed file the index holds and the codeReview.freshness handler queues one file job for it per mtime, after settling files with mtime 0 first; a file still stale after its request stays stale, so the existing time-out reaches the degraded diff review.
pros: Fixes the cause: the index stays current for every consumer, not only for a review
Reuses the existing handlers, queue and file job; no new storage
The gate's request covers what the watcher cannot know about (a restart gap, a failed watch)
A file the index cannot index is never declared fresh, so a failure still reaches the degraded diff review
cons: Two changes in two modules instead of one
Each such directory is watched twice, which uses more inotify watches

alternativesConsidered.name: Watcher fix only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Only the watcher changes; the freshness gate stays read-only.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The Watcher watches and scans new directories as in a1; the freshness compute and handler do not change.
pros: Smallest change to the review path
cons: Leaves the gate unable to recover from any other missed event, including a failed watch
A review of files the daemon missed while it was down still waits for the time-out and degrades
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the cause but leaves the gate unable to recover from a failed watch or a restart gap; partial on the second fix criterion.

alternativesConsidered.name: Gate request only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Leave the watcher alone and let the freshness gate request indexing of stale files.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The freshness compute lists every stale held file and the handler queues one file job per mtime; the watcher is unchanged.
pros: Small and contained to the review path
cons: Does not fix the cause: the unwatched directories stay unwatched, so everything else that relies on the index stays stale for files in them until a restart
Every review of such files pays a queue round trip
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A workaround that leaves the cause, which the user named as the crux; it violates the first fix criterion.

alternativesConsidered.name: Re-subscribe the whole repo when a nested directory appears, plus the gate request
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: On a created directory that has subdirectories, replace the repo's watch with a new one and scan the new tree.
alternativesConsidered.approach: On a create event for a directory with subdirectories, the Watcher unsubscribes the repo's subscription, subscribes again and scans the new directory; the gate request from a1 is kept. Events that occur between the unsubscribe and the new subscription are lost.
pros: No second subscription per directory, so no doubled watches
Re-establishes every watch under the repo
cons: A window with no watch on the whole repo while it re-subscribes, so events in it are lost
A full tree walk by the watcher backend on each such directory
Needs more bookkeeping to run for several directories at once
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Trades the doubled watches for a window in which the whole repo is unwatched, which is the kind of loss this Story removes; partial on the first fix criterion.

openQuestions: Graded partial in the audit (ts1): the Story record has no acceptance criteria; ac1 to ac9 were written in this LLD from the approved issue, the review rounds and the user's decision to bring the watcher into scope. The user confirmed the LLD as the acceptance baseline on 2026-10-27.

Graded partial in the audit (alt2): the Story has no acceptance criteria, Epic constraints or HLD contracts, so the three scored constraints were taken from the approved issue's fix intent and the user's decision on the watcher; the user confirmed this basis on 2026-10-27.

The approved ISSUE's root cause says the missing watcher event was not established, and its reproduction step 3 and second cause describe a wait deadlock that does not exist; the ISSUE record has not been revised to match the confirmed cause.
No test forces the per-directory subscribe call itself to fail; the unreadable-directory test covers the scan and the no-throw guarantee only.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How a directory created together with its parent gets its own watch and a scan so its files reach the index, and how a review's freshness poll then asks for any file still stale to be indexed and re-reads the queue so the same reply shows the work.

participants.label: File system
participants.description: A directory is created together with its parent and files are written into it

participants.label: Watcher
participants.description: Holds the repo subscription and the per-directory subscriptions

participants.label: Indexer
participants.description: Turns file events into file jobs on the queue

participants.label: codeReview.freshness handler
participants.description: Runs the compute, queues the index request and re-reads the queue

participants.label: IndexQueue
participants.description: Holds file jobs and reports code index work

messages.label: create event for the new directory
messages.description: The repo subscription reports the directory, not the nested ones created with it

messages.label: subscribe to the directory, then scan its tree
messages.description: The own subscription is created first so no write between the two steps is lost

messages.label: create events for the files present, then later writes
messages.description: Same event shape as the repo subscription's events

messages.label: file jobs
messages.description: The queue keeps one job per path

messages.label: enqueue a file job for each stale file the index holds
messages.description: Once per mtime, after settling files with mtime 0 and files the index never holds

messages.label: codeIndexWorkFor(repo)
messages.description: Re-reads the queue after the jobs were queued

messages.label: FreshnessResult with isProcessing true
messages.description: A file still stale after its request stays stale until the freshness time-out sends the review to the degraded diff review
